turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith stops just inside the door and doesn't sit. She sets her bag on the nearest desk and glances at the clock over your shoulder.

"Mr. Hale? Meredith Kalinowski. I have until 4:35.

Owen found out about this from the online gradebook, on his phone, during class. Who decided that was how he'd be told?"

She waits.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.

"You didn't answer my question. I'll want that in an email.

Fine. Before we read anything, I need to see three documents.

The checker report itself, with the date it was run. The policy on AI use for this assignment, in writing, and the date students received it. And whatever shows Owen was asked about this before the zero went in.

Was he?"

She pulls a pen from her bag and stays standing.
You're very sharp, you know that?

"I'm a parent who wants to see the documents. That's not sharp.

You're also still not answering. Was Owen asked about this before the zero was entered? Yes or no."

She uncaps the pen and looks at the desk, then at you.

"If the answer's no, say so. I'd rather have that than a compliment."
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.

"What timestamp issue?"

She stops with the pen over the page.

"I asked for the date the report was run. I haven't seen the report. If there's an issue with a timestamp, you've seen something I haven't. Show me."

She holds out her hand, palm up.

"And I'd still like an answer on whether Owen was asked before that zero went in."
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.

"'Had to.'" She says it flatly, the way you did. "Under which rule?

A flag and a zero aren't the same thing. Flagging is one step. Entering a zero in the gradebook before Owen has said a word is another. Which policy required you to do the second one?"

She lowers her hand and sets the pen on the desk.

"You've now complimented me three times and shown me nothing. I have a call at 4:40. The report, Mr. Hale. Or tell me you don't have it."
